items.claim: 10:28's joy/perish outcome bicolon is correctly held as a standalone verse; neither cited boundary conceals an undisclosed catchword tie.
items.evidence: 10:27-10:28 share only the common plural רשעים ("the wicked"), which sweeps to 42 verses book-wide (skeleton tier) and carries no diagnostic weight in a stretch built on righteous/wicked antithesis; 10:28-10:29 share zero skeleton content tokens. Both neighbors are cited in boundary_evidence_refs (web:Prov.10.27, web:Prov.10.29), and the gloss matches the pointed text at oshb:Prov.10.28: תּוֹחֶ֣לֶת צַדִּיקִ֣ים שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְתִקְוַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֹּאבֵֽד.

items.claim: 10:30's land-tenure bicolon is correctly isolated; the token it shares with 10:31 is the book's single most frequent righteous/wicked noun, not a boundary-worthy catchword.
items.evidence: 10:30-10:31 share only צדיק ("the righteous"), which sweeps to 66 verses book-wide (skeleton tier, exact singular form) and recurs constantly through the antithetic run in chs 10-15; 10:29-10:30 share no skeleton content token. Both boundary neighbors are cited (web:Prov.10.29, web:Prov.10.31), consistent with the row's own land-tenure vs. fortification/speech-organ topic distinctions.

items.claim: The תהפכות/construct-chain cluster evidence is sound, but boundary_evidence_refs discloses only the cluster's back boundary and leaves the forward boundary against 11:1 uncited.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel תהפכות confirms exactly 9 book-wide hits (Prov.2.12, 2.14, 6.14, 8.13, 10.31, 10.32, 16.28, 16.30, 23.33), and Prov.10.31-Prov.10.32 is the ONLY adjacent pair among them; the construct-chain opening is verified at oshb:Prov.10.31 (פִּֽי צַ֭דִּיק) / oshb:Prov.10.32 (שִׂפְתֵ֣י צַ֭דִּיק) -- the cluster call itself is well-grounded. But boundary_evidence_refs lists only web:Prov.10.30; web:Prov.11.1, the cluster's end-boundary neighbor, is never cited or argued against, so the row's own evidence does not carry both boundaries. Re-derivation finds no suppressed risk (10:32-11:1 share no exact skeleton content token; the nearest candidate, רצון/רצונו, changes spelling at the final nun and totals only 8+6=14 verses book-wide with no shared construction), so this is a completeness defect, not a miscall.
tier_citations: skeleton-tier sweep (sweep.py --skel רצון, 8 verses; --skel רצונו, 6 verses)

items.claim: 11:1's commerce-scale bicolon is correctly isolated at the chapter opening; both boundaries are cited and no undisclosed catchword links it to 10:32 or 11:2.
items.evidence: 10:32-11:1 share no exact skeleton content token (the nearest candidate, רצון/רצונו, changes final-letter spelling across the pair and rests on a moderate 8+6=14-verse book-wide root with no disclosed construction link); 11:1-11:2 likewise share none. Both neighbors are cited (web:Prov.10.32, web:Prov.11.2), and the gloss matches oshb:Prov.11.1: מֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭רְמָה ... וְאֶ֖בֶן שְׁלֵמָ֣ה.
tier_citations: skeleton-tier sweep (sweep.py --skel רצון, 8 verses; --skel רצונו, 6 verses)

items.claim: The exclusive צדקת construct-opening pair is real and sufficient for the cluster, but the claimed shared "3mp-suffix" template misstates 11:5's grammar, which is singular throughout.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel צדקת confirms exactly 2 book-wide hits, both this adjacent pair (Prov.11.5, Prov.11.6) -- solid, exclusive cluster grounds standing on their own. But 11:5's pronominal/verbal forms are 3ms, not 3mp: דַּרְכּ֑וֹ ("his way"), וּ֝בְרִשְׁעָת֗וֹ ("in his wickedness"), and יִפֹּ֥ל ("he falls") all agree with the singular subjects (oshb:Prov.11.5: צִדְקַ֣ת תָּ֭מִים תְּיַשֵּׁ֣ר דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְרִשְׁעָת֗וֹ יִפֹּ֥ל רָשָֽׁע); only 11:6 is plural -- תַּצִּילֵ֑ם ("delivers THEM") and יִלָּכֵֽדוּ ("they are trapped") agree with plural subjects (oshb:Prov.11.6: צִדְקַ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים תַּצִּילֵ֑ם וּ֝בְהַוַּ֗ת בֹּגְדִ֥ים יִלָּכֵֽדוּ). The "run consecutively across both verses" template claim overstates the parallelism, and the "high" confidence rating built partly on it is inflated.

items.claim: 11:7's isolation from 11:6 is correct on construct-chain grounds, but rejected_alternative repeats the same inaccurate "3mp-suffix" characterization of 11:5-11:6 used to justify the exclusion.
items.evidence: The verse-initial exclusion argument (11:7 lacks the צדקת-opening, oshb:Prov.11.7: בְּמ֤וֹת אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע תֹּאבַ֣ד תִּקְוָ֑ה וְתוֹחֶ֖לֶת אוֹנִ֣ים אָבָֽדָה) is sound on its own and does not depend on suffix number. But the row's supporting clause, describing the "3mp-suffix verb pattern that binds 11:5-11:6 together," is inaccurate: 11:5's suffixed/verbal forms (דַּרְכּ֑וֹ, וּ֝בְרִשְׁעָת֗וֹ, יִפֹּ֥ל) are 3ms, not 3mp (oshb:Prov.11.5); only 11:6 carries 3mp forms (תַּצִּילֵ֑ם, יִלָּכֵֽדוּ, oshb:Prov.11.6).

items.claim: 11:8 and 11:9 share the sole occurrence in the entire book of the root חלץ (Niphal, "delivered"), applied to the righteous in both verses -- undisclosed cross-seam cohesion that the row's rejected_alternative wrongly denies.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel חלץ (final-tsade spelling) returns exactly 1 hit, Prov.11.8 (נֶחֱלָ֑ץ, "is delivered"); sweep.py --skel חלצ (medial-tsade spelling) returns exactly 1 hit, Prov.11.9 (יֵחָלֵֽצוּ, "are delivered") -- together the ONLY two occurrences of this root anywhere in Proverbs, both Niphal, both predicated of the righteous (oshb:Prov.11.8: צַ֭דִּיק מִצָּרָ֣ה נֶחֱלָ֑ץ וַיָּבֹ֖א רָשָׁ֣ע תַּחְתָּֽיו; oshb:Prov.11.9: בְּפֶ֗ה חָ֭נֵף יַשְׁחִ֣ת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וּ֝בְדַ֗עַת צַדִּיקִ֥ים יֵחָלֵֽצוּ). This exclusivity is at least as strong as the construction-run evidence that grounded the 10:31-10:32 and 11:5-11:6 cluster calls elsewhere in this stretch, yet neither 11:8 nor 11:9 discloses it. The row's rejected_alternative states 11:9 "finds nothing to match" 11:8, which is byte-false.
tier_citations: skeleton-tier sweep (sweep.py --skel חלץ, 1 verse; --skel חלצ, 1 verse)

items.claim: 11:9 shares the book's only other occurrence of the root חלץ with its own back-neighbor 11:8, but the row's rejected_alternative addresses only the weaker forward neighbor, 11:10.
items.evidence: יֵחָלֵֽצוּ (oshb:Prov.11.9, "they are delivered," Niphal 3mp) and נֶחֱלָ֑ץ (oshb:Prov.11.8, "is delivered," Niphal 3ms) are the ONLY two attestations of the root חלץ in Proverbs (sweep.py --skel חלץ / חלצ, 1+1 verses), both predicated of the righteous. boundary_evidence_refs cites web:Prov.11.8, but rejected_alternative never engages it, instead defending only against 11:10 (whose shared צדיקים is the common plural, 23 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) -- the strongest real rival for this row is 11:8, not 11:10, and it goes unaddressed.
tier_citations: skeleton-tier sweep (sweep.py --skel חלץ, 1 verse; --skel חלצ, 1 verse)
